beats.intro: Chapter forty-two. [[sub]]Probability measures how likely something is to happen, with a number from zero to one.
beats.terms: Start with a few words. [[act]]The action is what you do: here, roll a number cube once. [[out]]The outcomes are all the possible results: one, two, three, four, five, or six. [[ev]]An event is an outcome or a group of outcomes, like rolling an even number. [[fav]]The outcomes in the event are the favorable ones: two, four, and six. [[eq]]On a fair cube, every face is equally likely to come up.
beats.formula: When the outcomes are equally likely, the probability of an event is a ratio. [[def]]The number of favorable outcomes, over the number of possible outcomes. [[num]]Three outcomes are even, [[den]]out of six possible outcomes. [[frac]]So the probability of rolling an even number is three sixths, [[simp]]which is one half, [[pct]]or fifty percent.
beats.scale: Every probability lands somewhere from zero to one. [[zero]]Rolling a seven can't happen: probability zero, impossible. [[one]]Rolling a number less than seven always happens: probability one, certain. [[half]]An even number is a fifty-fifty chance: one half. [[six]]Rolling a six is unlikely: one sixth, closer to zero. [[more]]Rolling more than one is likely: five sixths, closer to one. [[pct]]The same scale in percents runs from zero to one hundred percent.
beats.q1: Quick check. Find a probability on the spinner.
beats.or: Now an event with the word or. [[ask]]What is the probability of landing on red or yellow? [[fav]]Count every section that is red or yellow: two red plus two yellow is four. [[frac]]Four out of eight is one half. [[why]]You can add the two counts because one spin can't land on red and yellow at the same time. [[spin]]Spin it, and half the sections would make the event happen.
beats.sample: Some actions have more than one stage. [[two]]Flip a coin twice. [[list]]List every possible result in order: heads heads, heads tails, tails heads, and tails tails. [[space]]This list of all possible outcomes is the sample space. [[order]]Heads tails and tails heads are different outcomes, because the first flip is different. [[hh]]Only one of the four outcomes is two heads, so the probability is one fourth, or twenty-five percent.
beats.tree: A tree diagram builds the sample space one stage at a time. [[coin]]Flip a coin: two branches, heads or tails. [[die]]Then roll a number cube: each branch splits into six. [[leaves]]Following every path gives twelve outcomes, from heads one to tails six. [[ev]]What's the probability of heads and a six? [[one]]Just one path out of twelve: one twelfth.
beats.q2: Quick check. Use the tree diagram.
beats.count: You don't always need to draw the whole tree. [[rule]]The counting principle says: if one choice can be made in a ways and a second in b ways, then both together can be made in a times b ways. [[shirts]]Four shirts [[pants]]and three pairs of pants [[grid]]make four times three, or twelve outfits. [[each]]Each shirt pairs with each pair of pants.
beats.coins: The rule extends to more stages. [[flip]]Flip a coin three times. [[branch]]Each flip doubles the number of paths: two, then four, then eight. [[mult]]So there are two times two times two, eight arrangements. [[warn]]Not two times three. Three flips means three factors of two.
beats.comp: The complement of an event is the event not happening. [[ex]]Winning and losing, or heads and tails. [[sum]]Together, an event and its complement cover every outcome, so their probabilities add up to one, or one hundred percent. [[rain]]If the chance of rain tomorrow is thirty percent, [[no]]the chance of no rain is one hundred minus thirty: seventy percent. [[spin]]On the spinner, the probability of blue is three eighths, so the probability of not blue is five eighths.
beats.wrap: To sum up. [[w1]]The probability of an event is favorable outcomes over possible outcomes, a number from zero to one. [[w2]]A table or a tree diagram lists the sample space. [[w3]]The counting principle multiplies the number of choices at each stage. [[w4]]An event and its complement add up to one. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
beats.finish: Well done. That's the end of chapter forty-two, probability.
